overview.headline: Comparing chemical equations for photosynthesis and chemosynthesis

keyPoints.point: Students learn that photosynthesis uses solar energy to turn carbon dioxide and water into sugar and oxygen.
keyPoints.quote: All photosynthetic organisms use solar energy to turn carbon dioxide and water into sugar (food) and oxygen.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that a common vent form of chemosynthesis found at hydrothermal vents uses hydrogen sulfide to produce food.
keyPoints.quote: One common form of chemosynthesis found at hydrothermal vents uses hydrogen sulfide.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that the conservation of matter means matter cannot be created or destroyed during chemical reactions.
keyPoints.quote: Remind students that the law of conservation of matter states that matter cannot be created or destroyed.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that both processes produce a sugar compound made of carbon, hydrogen and oxygen as food.
keyPoints.quote: Both include a compound made of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen as a product (1:2:1) = simple sugar = food.

keyTerms.gloss: process that converts carbon dioxide into sugars using energy from the sun
keyTerms.quote: Photosynthesis: The process used by plants to convert carbon dioxide and water into oxygen and sugars (food), using energy from the sun.

keyTerms.gloss: process where microbes create sugars using energy released from chemical reactions
keyTerms.quote: Chemosynthesis: The process by which microbes create sugars (food) using energy released from chemical reactions.

keyTerms.gloss: organisms able to make their own food from raw materials and energy
keyTerms.quote: Autotroph: Organisms that are able to make their own food from raw materials and energy, also known as producers.

keyTerms.gloss: organisms that consume producers or other consumers for energy
keyTerms.quote: Heterotroph: Organisms that consume producers or other consumers, also known as consumers.

keyTerms.gloss: substance that changes during a chemical reaction as starting material
keyTerms.quote: Reactants: A substance that changes in a chemical reaction.
